messages.body_plain:
Hi,

Sorry for the late reaction – I re-ran the analysis in the meantime, and the problem disappeared. The only thing I changed was to lower the minimum for a branch to be treated as direct ancestors – which apparently was the case for two branches in the previous analysis. However I don't know if this can explain why two different likelihood values are returned at the end.

Best – Jan

On Sat, Nov 26, 2016 at 1:58 AM, Jan Hackel <jan.h...@univ-tlse3.fr> wrote:

> Hello,
>
> I have a question regarding the (log) total Maximum Likelihood value of a BioGeoBEARS estimation: I used to retrieve it from the model output as saved to a .Rdata file, such as "res$total_loglikelihood" (-407 in my case). Now I realised, for a time-stratified analysis, that this value is not the same as the one one reported on screen at the end of the estimation (-380, = the value reported from optimx, column "value"). Am I right in assuming that these should be the same and correspond to the total log-likelihood? In that case, how come in my case they are different? Or do they refer to different things? Might it be a convergence issue (but the optimx output reports successful convergence)?
>
> I based my model comparison by AIC on the values obtained from $total_loglikelihood for each model so far, but now I am a bit confused... Can anyone help me?
>
> Thanks – Jan

messages.body_plain:
Ah!  That could do it, if e.g. the time-stratification process creates a really really short branch (because time-stratification basically takes the input tree and chops it into a bunch of little trees).

The other thing I was thinking about is the root branch, most trees don't have root branches, but the time-stratification analyses use them (because a subtree has to extend to the bottom of a time bin).

Glad you figured it out!

Cheers!
Nick

messages.subject: Results interpretation - difference between corner node and its next node
messages.subject_clean: Results interpretation - difference between corner node and its next node
messages.body_plain:
Hello!

I am not sure to understand how to interpret the results of my DEC+j analysis. If we take the example in the attached file, we have node 1 with blue for the most probable area. In next corner node (2), we should have the areas just after cladogenesis. Here the most probable area is red, so we have an hypothesis of founder event speciation from blue to red, have we ?

My trouble is after: I don't understand what happens between 2 and 3. Is it normal that the estimates could change? Does it mean that in another study I could estimate range expansion or diminution between a corner node and the next node? So between the speciation and the diversification?

In my analysis, as the probabilities between red and green are close and that green area is a little island, I will probably hypothesize that the dispersal and the diversification occured in red area, but in another situation it could be more disturbing.

Thank you very much if someone can light me on this! :)

Lucie

messages.body_plain:
I'm traveling but... those pie charts mostly mean you have a lot of uncertainty under that model. Maybe another model would work better. Anyway, for any particular model, Biogeographical Stochastic Mapping will give you a sample of possible exact histories

Be very very sure you understand the difference between ancestral range probabilities and an exact history, this is very very commonly misunderstood by people who seem to naturally think in a parsimony fashion. Read the "mistakes not to make" page on the BioGeoBEArS phylowiki.

Indeed, I did not do the difference...*shame*

For the model, DEC+j was the one with the smallest AIC value, but I observed only 2.4 points of difference with the next more probable model (DIVALIKE+j) and the probabilities are very similar between the two models.

I will test BSM to see the sample of possible exact histories, but given the uncertainties on the pie charts it will be probably hard to propose a clear biogeographic history of my group. Is there a way to select the most probable history under several BSM results? I know it won't be accurate to present a single history, but it could be used as a starting point to compare with the different histories sampled?

Thank you!

On Fri, Dec 9, 2016 at 11:25 AM, Lucie <lucie....@gmail.com> wrote:
> Indeed, I did not do the difference...*shame*

> For the model, DEC+j was the one with the smallest AIC value, but I observed only 2.4 points of difference with the next more probable model (DIVALIKE+j) and the probabilities are very similar between the two models.
>
> I will test BSM to see the sample of possible exact histories, but given the uncertainties on the pie charts it will be probably hard to propose a clear biogeographic history of my group. Is there a way to select the most probable history under several BSM results? I know it won't be accurate to present a single history, but it could be used as a starting point to compare with the different histories sampled?
>

Hi -- your real Bayesian estimate *is* the sample of histories.  What I would do is run some BSM and then summarize the various scenarios in a table or something, e.g. 13% this history, 20% this history, etc.  But, with those pie charts, you won't get a lot of resolution.

If you really want to clarify the history, you probably need more data/more outgroups etc., methods can only help so much.

As for the single best history...these are not the droids you are looking for:
http://phylo.wikidot.com/biogeobears-mistakes-to-avoid#joint_histories

Cheers!
Nick

Hello,

I am a beginner in R, so I called some masters.

With a FOR loop, I obtained the stats for my ingroup nodes alone, here the code if someone else is interested:

clado_events_tablesAlt = list()
for (i in 1:100){
clado_events_tablesAlt[[i]] = clado_events_tables[[i]][30:43,]}
clado_events_tables = clado_events_tablesAlt

ana_events_tablesAlt = list()
for (i in 1:100){
ana_events_tablesAlt[[i] = ana_events_tables[[i]][30:43,]}
ana_events_tables = ana_events_tablesAlt

#and then I continued with the tutorial (I only changed the pdf name):

# Simulate the source areas
BSMs_w_sourceAreas = simulate_source_areas_ana_clado(res, clado_events_tables, ana_events_tables, areanames)
clado_events_tables = BSMs_w_sourceAreas$clado_events_tables
ana_events_tables = BSMs_w_sourceAreas$ana_events_tables

# Count all anagenetic and cladogenetic events
counts_list = count_ana_clado_events(clado_events_tables, ana_events_tables, areanames, actual_names)

summary_counts_BSMs = counts_list$summary_counts_BSMs
